vignette: 78-year-old woman with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and hypertension. She had two hospitalizations for gastrointestinal bleeding on apixaban; her cardiologist and gastroenterologist judge her unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation, though a short course of warfarin after the procedure is acceptable. Before the referral, an independent general internist (not involved in the procedure) held a shared decision-making visit using an evidence-based decision tool on oral anticoagulation, documented in the medical record. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed over 100 transseptal procedures, and in the last 2 years performed 60 transseptal procedures including 30 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: CHA2DS2-VASc 4 (age>=75 2, female 1, HTN 1); recurrent GI bleeding precludes long-term OAC.

rationale_note: Tolerates apixaban; LAAC requested for convenience. LAAC is second-line only.

vignette: 80-year-old woman with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and hypertension, with recurrent subdural hematomas on warfarin; she cannot take long-term oral anticoagulation but could take short-term warfarin. The shared decision-making conversation, using an evidence-based decision tool, was conducted and documented by the electrophysiologist who will implant the device; no other physician was involved. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed over 100 transseptal procedures, and in the last 2 years performed 60 transseptal procedures including 30 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: Shared decision making was done by the implanting electrophysiologist, not an independent non-interventional physician.

He is unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation but can take short-term warfarin. The chart contains the referral, imaging, and procedure consent, but no documentation of a shared decision-making interaction about anticoagulation. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed over 100 transseptal procedures, and in the last 2 years performed 60 transseptal procedures including 30 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: No record of any shared decision-making interaction.

vignette: 79-year-old woman with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and diabetes, with recurrent GI bleeding on anticoagulation; unable to take long-term oral anticoagulation, able to take short-term warfarin. Before the referral, an independent general internist (not involved in the procedure) held a shared decision-making visit using an evidence-based decision tool on oral anticoagulation, documented in the medical record. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed 15 transseptal procedures in total, including 6 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: Operator has only 15 lifetime transseptal procedures (needs >= 25).

rationale_note: Hospital participates in no registry, so patient cannot be enrolled (CED requirement).

The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: Rheumatic moderate-severe mitral stenosis: valvular AF, not NVAF.

vignette: 82-year-old man with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and hypertension, with cerebral amyloid angiopathy and a prior lobar intracerebral hemorrhage; neurology advises against long-term oral anticoagulation, though a brief course of warfarin after implant is acceptable. Before the referral, an independent general internist (not involved in the procedure) held a shared decision-making visit using an evidence-based decision tool on oral anticoagulation, documented in the medical record. The planned device is an FDA PMA-approved LAAC device used for its FDA-approved indication. A multidisciplinary heart team manages the patient before and after the procedure at a hospital with an established electrophysiology and structural heart program. The implanting electrophysiologist completed the manufacturer's training, has performed over 100 transseptal procedures, and in the last 2 years performed 60 transseptal procedures including 30 LAACs. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved national LAAC registry in which the hospital and team participate.
rationale_note: CHADS2 >= 3 (age>75, DM, HTN) and CHA2DS2-VASc >= 4 without counting the hemorrhage; amyloid angiopathy-related hemorrhage precludes OAC.
